concept: A handcrafted paper-cutout stop motion of Hercules clashing with the Lernaean Hydra in a marsh diorama, built from layered cardstock and vellum under a fixed lamp.
style_bible: Layered paper-cutout stop motion photographed on a tabletop diorama rig under a locked-off camera. Constructed from cold-press cardstock with visible tooth, layered brown kraft paper for terrain and muscle mass, shredded crepe paper for fur and tongue details, translucent vellum for necks and mist, and iron-grey board for the club. Every layer stands three millimetres in front of the next, casting a soft contact shadow onto the plane behind. Edges are hand-cut with a craft knife, crisp but slightly irregular, showing a pale paper core where coloured stock is cut through. Sheets curl and warp a little, registration is a hair imperfect, and motion is animated on twos. All tone comes from stacked cut shapes — no digital gradients, no 3D render, no plastic sheen, no airbrushing. Hercules: tall, broad-shouldered figure built from layered parchment white and bog brown cardstock, draped in a lion pelt of shredded tan crepe paper fastened with visible brass split pins at shoulders and hips; face is matte black cardstock with punched eye holes revealing dark indigo underlayer, mouth a sharp angled slit; wears torn trousers of deep indigo board with a jagged tear along the left hem; holds a heavy club cut from iron-grey board with sandpaper-textured residue. The Lernaean Hydra: seven serpentine heads mounted on long necks of layered translucent vellum and moss green paper, bodies coiled from brown kraft; eyes are glossy black pin-head beads, tongues forked strips of wine red crepe; joints visible as brass pins at neck bases; center head bears a charred black edge. Environment: receding planes of storm slate-blue felt-backed cardstock for water, stacked bog brown rock formations in background, upper third filled with pale grey vellum haze sheets. Palette: storm slate-blue, deep indigo, bog brown, moss green, parchment white, iron grey, charred black. Lighting rig: warm key from upper left casting long soft shadows to the right, cool fill from lower right, raking across paper tooth to catch layer edges and registration hairlines. Framing: vertical 9:16 portrait.
